a precision NMR crossed‐coil polarimeter has been developed to measure the polarization of a frozen HD sample.
we have built and tested a crossed‐coil polarimeter with a precision of 4%, and have demonstrated that the nonideal behavior of the polarimeter does not limit the precision of this instrument.
a precision NMR circuit can be designed that can measure proton and deuteron polarizations with an uncertainty of 4%.

the development of precision NMR instrumentation for use in polarimetry and magnetometry.
the development of an NMR polarimeter with the precision required to measure the polarization of the LEGS frozen spin HD targets used in photoprodution experiments.
the development of a new precision NMR polarimetry technique for use in nuclear physics experiments.

the precision HD polarimeter has been shown to be a very useful tool for the study of polarized HD targets.
the precision NMR polarimetry technique is a robust and reliable method for the measurement of polarization.

the polarimeter is capable of detecting a 0.1% polarization with a 5% uncertainty, and a 1% polarization with less than a 1% uncertainty.
the LEGS polarimeter has achieved a precision in polarization measurements of 0.1% for the proton and 0.2% for the deuteron, with a time resolution of 10 min.

the crossed‐coil polarimeter is an extremely robust instrument that can maintain its performance over the long term.
a polarimeter can be designed to be as precise as the target itself.
